summary: Phase 149O.20L.5 -- Class-B Real Host Provisioning Authorization & Planning. PLANNING/AUTHORIZATION-BOUNDARY ONLY -- no production, contract, or real host change. With CBV-S1 and CBV-S10 (the only two genuinely-triggered Class-B architectural stop conditions) independently reconfirmed closed and not reopened, re-derived docs/PHASE_149O_20H_CLASS_B_DEPLOYMENT_VERIFIER_MODEL_A_ENVIRONMENT_LOCK_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md §32 (Real Authorization Boundaries) and §33 (Stop Conditions) directly from primary source, not from any intervening phase's summary, and re-read HBDC-001 v1.0's full 55-requirement text directly. Re-invoked verify_class_b_deployment_conformance() and assess_hatp_mandatory_activation_readiness() live, unmocked, read-only against this actual development host: NON_COMPLIANT / ready=False, git status confirmed clean immediately after every call. Captured the complete 23-item live NON_COMPLIANT reason inventory and mapped every one to a real-host mutation category (OS-principal creation; Protected Root creation and ACL/group/ancestor-chain configuration; admin-owned production Python-environment provisioning covering interpreter/venv/site/customization/.pth/launcher; trusted-git launch-PATH configuration -- 9 bundled real actions, each with purpose/privilege/precondition/postcondition/verification/rollback) or to an observation-only condition not fixable by provisioning alone (pcae_distribution_metadata_not_found packaging condition; CRI Layer 1 repository-identity bootstrap, which is explicitly agent-writable-by-design and unrelated to Class-B topology). Performed direct, read-only host-eligibility inspection (uname/sw_vers, dscl/id principal enumeration, stat-based ownership of the repo/.venv/Homebrew install/user-site/editable .pth pointer, live PATH ordering) and determined this development workstation is NOT eligible as the Class-B provisioning target as currently configured: a single OS principal (this developer's own account) owns every candidate admin-controlled resource, including this repository's own editable-install .pth pointer -- HBDC-REQ-026 itself explicitly rejects a developer-writable repo-local .venv as compliant regardless of source-tree certification status. Recommended (not decided) a dedicated deployment host/environment instead, reasoning that provisioning in place would either break ordinary development on this machine or require a parallel admin-owned environment alongside the existing one. Defined and textually separated three distinct boundaries: Boundary P (provisioning authorization, this phase's own scope), Boundary A (real HATP_MANDATORY activation), and Boundary C (HMIC certification, independently derived as a third necessary boundary from scripts/hatp_certification_admin.py's own certify/activate/revoke command separation) -- no future authorization from this plan's own proposition may collapse any of them into another. Reconstructed the repository's own GPC6-REQ-075(b) human-authority-election precedent (docs/GPC6_REQ_075B_HUMAN_AUTHORITY_ELECTION.md, read directly) as the working model for what an explicit human authorization record must contain (first-person, dated, signed, explicit non-extension list, explicit confirmation sentence) and determined that PCAE's own subsequently-built CHGR-001 canonical-human-governance-record mechanism (pcae decision-session create/evidence/select/clarify/preview/confirm/readiness -> pcae governance-record publish/inspect/verify, all independently confirmed present and callable in the live CLI) is the correct, already-implemented reusable authorization artifact for a future Boundary-P election -- no competing mechanism was invented. Drafted the exact Boundary-P authorization proposition text a human governance authority would later elect on: host/source/plan-digest bound, naming exactly the nine planned actions, one-shot per this repository's own narrow-authority precedent, and explicitly excluding HMIC certification and real HATP_MANDATORY activation. Designed dependency ordering (OS principal as sole root prerequisite, two independent downstream branches for Protected Root and environment lock, final read-only aggregate re-verification), partial-failure semantics (fail-closed, re-verify already-completed steps rather than blind rollback of everything), idempotency (inspect-compare-mutate-if-needed-verify per step, reusing the exact already-implemented read-only verifier functions), and a preflight stage (collision detection, target-path-absence confirmation, host-eligibility re-check) -- none of it executed by this phase. Independently confirmed, by direct inspection of the actual call graph, that no step in the provisioning command plan calls activate_hatp_mandatory, any hatp_mandatory_certification.py write path, or any Cutover Record mutation, and that provisioning completion is a structural stop (no automatic chaining into certification or activation). This document's own companion test file (tests/test_phase_149o_20l_5_class_b_real_host_provisioning_authorization_and_planning.py, 12 tests) verifies, using a fresh isolated-subprocess re-invocation of the real verifier (avoiding pytest's own assertion-rewrite meta_path finder polluting the HBDC-REQ-032 check): every live-captured NON_COMPLIANT requirement ID is present in the planning document's own mutation-mapping table; every mutation-classed row cites a real HBDC-REQ-### ID; no provisioning-plan step contains an activation/certification call; the authorization-proposition text explicitly excludes activation and certification; Boundary P and Boundary A are textually distinct and explicitly stated as never combined; the explicit non-authorizations section covers every required exclusion; the phase-exit banner states NOT PROVISIONED/NOT READY, never COMPLIANT; and git status shows only this phase's own new, still-unstaged planning artifacts throughout -- no unexpected mutation. No real provisioning, certification, or activation was authorized or performed by this phase. Recommends exactly one next phase: 149O.20L.6 -- Class-B Provisioning Authorization Record Capture (publish or decline the CHGR encoding this phase's own §29 proposition; still no provisioning). Not begun by this phase.
